identity.description:
Count an obvious one-line fix as a subagent item

## Summary

The orchestrator now gives an obvious one-line fix to a subagent with no word from the principal. Before, the test kept every change to code, a test, a config or an instruction file with an implementer. That cost time and tokens on work that needs no project lead. The test now says what "obvious" means, and which one-line changes still go to an implementer.

**Ticket:** N/A, the principal's word: "yes obvious one-liners should also count as a subagent item"
**Type:** New feature. Plugin version 0.1.129.

---

## Agent context

### Authority

`docs/design.md` §15.157 and the new finding §15.161. `skills/orchestrator/references/subagent-items.md` owns the test.

### What changed, by file

- `skills/orchestrator/references/subagent-items.md`: part 3 passes an obvious one-line fix; a definition of "obvious"; new example rows; a section "The one-line fix" with what the subagent does before its ready line; the diff check before the merge for a one-line fix.
- `docs/design.md`: new §15.161 finding, and a pointer in §15.157's decision.

### Constraints that applied

No rule has a second copy: a grep of `skills/`, `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/design.md` found no other statement of part 3. The plugin `version` is 0.1.129 in `plugin.json` and `marketplace.json`. The finding is §15.161.

### How this was verified

Read the file and the files that point at it against `writing-standard.md`.

### Known gaps

No orchestrator run has judged an item by the new part 3.

change in another file, other than the test.

- **A value that every PR changes.** Examples: a version number, or a
  sequence number in a design doc. You own it. Assign it to each PR, in merge
  order, when that PR is next to merge.

- A change to what the plugin loads — `agents/`, `skills/`, `hooks/`, or the
  manifests — bumps `version` in both `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and
  `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`.

The new merge check allows only "the one line and at most its test" and "no change in another file", and it makes no exception for those values. So a literal reading sends every one-line fix to an instruction file to "Larger than it looked".
